reasoning: According to Congressional Research Service (CRS) records and historical budget data, Congress has enacted all of its regular annual appropriations bills before the start of the fiscal year (October 1) only four times since the modern budget process was established under the Congressional Budget Act of 1974: for Fiscal Years 1977, 1989, 1995, and 1997. Since FY 1997 (enacted in late 1996), Congress has not passed a complete, regular budget with all full-year appropriations bills enacted on time, relying instead on continuing resolutions (CRs) and late omnibus funding packages.
title: US Congress passed no budget on time since 1997
